title: Sampled callsite trace profiles and cost decomposition widget
author: Sofia Reyes
description:
Motivation: long-tail token cost and tail latency often correlate with particular callsites in user code (prompt patterns, tool calls). Current sampling is either coarse (per-invocation) or heavy (full-trace capture) which increases cost and makes dashboarding noisy. This PR introduces a lightweight callsite-aware sampling layer that attaches compact 'trace profile' anchors to representative invocations and a new cost-decomposition dashboard widget that surfaces per-callsite token/latency contribution across recent windows.

What this implements: 1) backend sampling engine (observability/sampling/callsite_sampler.go) that computes and persists small trace anchors (callsite signature, token count, phase timings) using reservoir sampling per-route and per-tenant. Sampling heuristics balance token-cost-weighted and entropy-guided selection so we capture both high-cost and high-variance callsites. 2) compact RPC and storage schema (telemetry/schema/callsite_profile_v1.yaml) and migration logic to retain backwards compatibility with existing invocation rollups. 3) frontend dashboard widget (ui/dashboard/widgets/cost_decomp_widget.tsx) that queries aggregated callsite profiles and renders an interactive stacked decomposition by token-phase (encode/attend/decode) and latency phase, with drilldowns into representative trace anchors. 4) alert tuning helpers: a new metric (observability/metrics/callsite_suspect_count) and an alert rule template (alerts/observability/callsite_alert_templates.yaml) that can be used to attach callsite-level suppression windows and quieting. 5) docs and runbook (docs/observability/callsite_profiles.md) describing how to interpret the widget and how to onboard routes to higher-fidelity sampling.

Backward compatibility and migration: the schema and query layer fall back to the existing invocation rollups when callsite profiles are not available. We added a short migration tool that backfills top-K callsite anchors from recent heavy invocations (runs as a low-priority job) — it is opt-in via an admin flag.

Tests and validation: unit tests for sampler selection logic and reservoir correctness; end-to-end integration test that simulates synthetic traffic shapes and validates widget aggregation. Performance: sampling layer adds ~0.7% CPU overhead at 95th percentile on our perf-canary (measured on p3-type nodes) and reduces full-trace capture volume by ~63% for large tenants in the replay bench. Dashboard query latency (90th) for the new widget is ~120ms for a 30m window after adding targeted indexes.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind 'callsite_profiles' per-tenant flag. Start with opt-in on redwood internal tenant and two beta customers for 2 weeks, then expand to early-access customers with communication and dashboard training.

Risks & mitigation: potential increase in cardinality due to callsite signature explosion — mitigated by shingle-based normalization and a top-K eviction policy per-route. Storage overhead is controlled by compact anchor format and TTL. Alerts can be noisy initially; included templates add auto-quiet windows and decay to avoid alert storms.

See related Linear tickets: ENG-1429 (callsite sampling design), ENG-1452 (dashboard widget), and support ticket SUP-8212 for early customer request.
